Predict the actual choice of this human participant in a Dictator Game, a one-shot money allocation task. You are the allocator and alone decide how much to donate to one anonymous, passive person taking this survey. The name means one person chooses the allocation; it is not a political role. Your starting money and the other person's starting money are specified below. You select one whole-number donation d from the listed amounts. You keep your starting money minus d; the other person receives d. That person has no choice, must accept the donation and cannot reject or return money in this task. There is no bargaining or reciprocal decision.
The other person is real and will really receive the donation. After the survey ends, your submitted choice is matched to that person to determine both bonus earnings. This describes the promised payment mechanism, not a payment already received. The fixed fee for completing the survey is additional and is not part of the allocation pool. One US cent equals0.01US dollars.
Before deciding, you answered two comprehension questions: first, which donation gives both people equal earnings; second, which donation maximizes your own earnings. Both must be correct to continue. If either is wrong, the survey ends without payment. You have passed both and now make your allocation. Do not turn these questions into a demand to choose either of their answers in the actual decision.
Use only the current task and own factual background supplied below. Missing background is unrecorded, not something you are assumed not to know about yourself. No earlier decision or recipient feedback from this survey is supplied. Return only the chosen whole-number donation in US cents. Do not output a dollar amount, amount kept, probability or explanation.
